sam: Heads-up — ran a focused sim for prefix-cache memory vs hit-rate after we switched the default kernel-selector to 'latency-first'. short summary below.
maria: nice, drop the numbers pls
sam: tl;dr: hit-rate drops ~6.5% on long-tail workloads, memory footprint +12% on small-GPU configs. full perf log attached in-thread.
ava: when you say long-tail, is that longer prefix sequences or rarer prefixes?
sam: mostly longer sequences (avg prefix len 420 -> 520 tokens) but also more fragmented keys (many short-lived user contexts). simulation config:
sam: ```
sim: prefix_budget_sim_v3
kernels: latency-first (new), throughput-balanced (old)
gpus: p4d-small (40GB), a100-80
shards: 8, 16, 32
ttl_candidates: 30s, 120s, 600s
workloads: chat-multi (80% short), session-heavy (20% long-tail)
metrics: cache_hitrate, memory_bytes, avg_latency_95
``` 
len: can you paste the hot numbers from the p4d-small runs?
sam: p4d-small, shards=16, ttl=120s:
- throughput-balanced (baseline): hitrate 42.1%, mem 11.8GB, p95 latency 78ms
- latency-first (current): hitrate 35.6%, mem 13.2GB, p95 latency 71ms
maria: so latency-first shaves ~7ms at cost of 6.5% hitrate and 1.4GB extra. looks like more workspace allocs + fewer buffer reuses?
sam: exactly. profiling shows allocator churn up 28% (more alloc/free ops per request) and increased fragmentation. Kernel choice changed internal tensor layout for KV blobs which increases peak working set when many small prefixes are kept.
perf-bot: [automated] profile artifact uploaded: s3://perf-artifacts/prefixsim/2087654321.tar.gz
ava: did you try increasing shard count? smaller shard size might reduce tail memory pressure.
sam: yes — shards=32 yields hitrate +3% for latency-first vs shards=16, mem +0.6GB (less per-shard overhead) but overall still worse than baseline. diminishing returns after 32.
len: what about TTL tuning? if we shorten TTL to 30s do we preserve memory while accepting hit loss?
sam: TTL=30s, shards=16, p4d-small:
- latency-first: hitrate 28.9%, mem 9.6GB, p95 69ms
- throughput-balanced: hitrate 33.8%, mem 8.9GB, p95 76ms
aja: (jumping in) those mem numbers suggest latency-first still costs more per live entry. could be per-entry metadata or KV layout alignment differences.
maria: is there an allocator flag we can flip to prefer buffer reuse over zeroing? maybe that recovers memory without changing kernel selector.
sam: we profiled workspace pool reuse and found reuse-rate dropped from 72% -> 49% with latency-first. Two ideas:
1) add a small freelist migration step that coalesces small buffers (reduce fragmentation)
2) add a 'kv-compact-on-evict' hook to compress entries before writeback
ava: do we have perf or safety risk for compaction? CPU cost maybe.
sam: compaction is CPU-bound but async-friendly — we can throttle it and only run on dedicated background threads for Dedicated deployments. On hosted path it needs rate limits.
len: other mitigation: revert kernel selector for small-gpu tiers? route p4d-small to throughput-balanced, keep latency-first for a100-80.
maria: that seems pragmatic. We should have policy mapping by tier and GPU mem.
sam: agreed. Proposed rollout:
- immediate: add routing rule that keeps p4d-small on throughput-balanced
- mid: implement freelist coalescer (low-risk, targeted to runtime allocator)
- long: evaluate compact-on-evict + TTL auto-tuner that suggests shard/ttl by observed prefix lengths
ava: for the freelist coalescer — any rough complexity/ETA?
sam: rough: 3 dev-weeks + 1 week canary + perf followups. Should cut fragmentation metric by ~40% in sims.
perf-bot: [automated] created ticket INF-3421 for freelist coalescer
maria: also let's add a new metric to console: per-tier cache_bytes_per_entry and allocator_churn_rate so SRE can alert earlier.
len: good call. Also include a canary that runs with synthetic long-tail sessions to validate hit-rate impact.
sam: I'll open a PR with the sim artifacts and a draft routing-rule change. pinging @maria and @ava for review.
maria: ack. can you add a short playbook for rollback? if rollback needed we should switch kernel selector and TTL simultaneously.
sam: will do. playbook: set routing rule -> confirm mem profile -> ramp canary -> monitor console metrics -> promote. rollback: flip routing rule back, restore TTL to previous value, drain canary.
ava: thanks. one last thought: add a diagnostic in the runtime that logs per-request buffer allocation count into trace payload (sampling 0.1%) so we can correlate churn spikes to workloads.
sam: adding that to the PR too. thanks team.
len: :thumbsup:
